attribution.note: Zitron's own words on his own blog, about his own earlier prediction.

semantics.note: He looks back and admits the OpenAI-dead-by-end-2025 call was a mistake. The normalised text matches that admission. Whether the 2024 forecast was really worded that way is a separate question.

contract.note: Reading 'dead' as no longer operating as a business is the ordinary meaning. The test asks for independent proof that OpenAI kept operating after 2025, which is fair.

evidence.note: A dated OpenAI disclosure from January 2026 describes active subscriptions, APIs and customers. It is a company disclosure, but it shows the business still operating after the deadline.
This is the admission itself. It records what he said and cannot prove the outcome.
The related July 2024 article hedged its collapse prediction. That raises a provenance question about the original forecast but does not touch whether OpenAI survived.

reviews.rationale: The passage plainly admits the prediction failed, and e1 shows OpenAI still running its business in January 2026, after the stated deadline. e3 shows the original 2024 wording was hedged, but the contract treats that as a separate provenance issue. The admission is accurate.

attribution.note: Zitron's own analysis in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Will now have to cover' is firm wording, so this is a scored forecast. The causal link to NVIDIA's price rises comes from the preceding sentence ('This means'). The 2027 delivery condition is kept.

contract.note: The contract reads 'any data center' as each facility facing at least $2B in extra cost. That follows the speaker's own universal wording, but it is strict, and the result depends on that choice.

evidence.note: Reuters relays Bloomberg: announced server price rises above 15% for systems shipping in early 2027. There are no completed deliveries and no facility-level dollar figures, and Reuters did not verify the report.

reviews.rationale: Deliveries that would qualify start in 2027, after the evaluation date, and the forecast has no end date. The packet holds only an announcement of percentage rises, not facility costs, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The claim cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in the essay's conclusion.

semantics.note: The 'may' applies only to the concession that the technology is more useful. The main clauses (not profitable enough, not reliable enough to be world-changing) are firm statements about the present. The sentence also implies a causal link.

contract.note: The ordinary reading is fair, but the speaker named no profit measure, company or threshold for 'world-changing'. The choice of Q2 2026 as the test period comes from the evaluator, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 for Q2 2026 shows $974M operating income but a $66B net loss (mostly fair-value changes), with operating losses in earlier quarters. That is not sustained full-cost profitability, but it does undercut a blanket claim. The profit measure is unspecified.
A preprint shows reliability failures in simulated document editing. Its narrow scope cannot settle whether LLMs are 'world-changing'.

reviews.rationale: On profitability, the evidence points both ways: one quarter of operating income against a large net loss, with no sustained profit and no stated measure. The reliability clause has no threshold, and one simulation study cannot test it. The packet does not settle either clause.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Will' is firm, so this is a forecast. The normalised text leaves out 'in the end', but that phrase sets no deadline, so the open horizon is effectively kept. The forecast assumes boosters were wrong.

contract.note: Reading the behaviour as denying or rewriting false claims, across many advocates, is a fair ordinary reading. The speaker defined no population, threshold or endpoint.

evidence.note: Altman admitting a mistake in May 2026 came before the forecast and is one person. It cannot confirm or refute a pattern among many boosters.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline ('in the end'), and the packet documents no pattern of boosters denying their errors after the essay was published. The early-resolution rule is not met. One earlier admission settles nothing.
